title: The Family Photograph With a Missing Name
short_teaser: Genealogists often identify unknown people by comparing dates, clothing, locations, and family relationships.
story: Genealogists often identify unknown people by comparing dates, clothing, locations, and family relationships. Identity can emerge from several modest clues rather than one decisive fact. Discovery begins when attention stays with what does not fit long enough for a better explanation to emerge. The value is not only knowing the story, but recognizing where the same pattern may already be present in ordinary life, creative work, or business.
